items.evidence: recursion is basically when your code calls itself
items.note: The student correctly defined recursion as a function calling itself.
The student stated that a recursive function requires a base case.
The student did not explain that the base case returns a result without further calls.
The student did not mention that each call operates on a strictly smaller subproblem.
The student mentions a new frame is pushed, but contradicts it with misconceptions about parallel execution and overwriting.

items.evidence: sometimes people forget and it overflows the stack
items.note: The student correctly noted that an absent base case triggers a stack overflow.
The student did not discuss rewriting recursion iteratively.
The student did not mention tail call optimization.

target_reason: Understanding what the base case does is essential to stop the recursion from running infinitely.
target_focus: what happens when the base case is reached
